leads.question: Run the SLOAD, SSTORE, TLOAD and TSTORE handlers, checkpoint, checkpoint_revert and JournalEntry::revert of world-chain v2.8.2 (op-stack-eth.work/dl/wc282/x/usr/local/bin/world-chain, with symbols; table 0x52f92a0 and the routines named in the theme-reth-journal-binary-lift lead) and of conduit-op-reth v2.5.1 (op-stack-eth.work/dl/conduit251/x/app/conduit-op-reth) through rethj.py with the op-reth nested-frame sequences. Does every inner revert restore the transient words of CurrencyDelta, NonzeroDeltaCount and CurrencyReserves and the persistent pool words?
leads.why: These two builds are the only OP Stack execution clients behind a PoolManager whose journal has never run, and World Chain's nightly compiler output differs from op-reth's. A revert that kept a transient credit (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:28-40, src/libraries/NonzeroDeltaCount.sol) while the token transfer rolled back would let any account settle in an inner frame, revert it and keep the credit, which takes pooled funds of every currency.

leads.question: Lift the SSTORE handler (with the gas check that moved between v1.19.1 and v1.19.2), the SLOAD database miss path and the storage credit accounting from the tempo v1.19.2 x86_64 binary in stablecoin-l1.work/dl, and run them in the cycle 28 x86-64 model on the PoolManager's slot shapes (pool slot0 and liquidity, tick and position words, protocolFeesAccrued, ERC-6909 balances) with reverts at depth 1 to 3. Do reads, original values and the written word equal pyevm.py after every revert?
leads.why: Tempo has one client and these are the last storage paths of the running build that were never executed from the binary. A wrong word written or restored on a reverted frame would change pool state for every LP, and any account can drive SSTORE at chosen depths through its own unlock callback.

leads.question: The images of celo-v1.0.10 (theme-reth-keccak-asm-image-lift.work/dl/celo-v1.0.10), xlayer-reth v0.0.7.3-rc.1 (dl/xlayer-rc1), reth-bsc v0.1.4 and v0.1.4-hotfix (dl/rethbsc-*) and arc-execution v0.8.5 and v0.8.6 are on disk, but only their keccak routines were lifted. Do their 25 arithmetic, comparison and shift handlers, EXP variants and analyze_legacy give the reference word in the cycle 32 x86-64 model on the 323,997 cases used for World Chain, and does any of them use BMI2, ADX or AVX on those paths?
leads.why: World Chain showed this cycle that a different compiler yields different handler code from the same crates. These four images were built by their own toolchains and are what the X Layer, Celo and Arc producers and the reth-bsc validators are said to run. A handler fault on an operand shape that the endpoint vectors miss would change FullMath, TickMath or BitMath results in every pool.

leads.question: In the cycle 33 census of 40,940 validated MegaETH blocks, how many of the SAR-of-negative, SIGNEXTEND-from-byte-3-to-30-with-sign, BYTE and SHL-by-256-or-more executions ran inside the PoolManager at 0xacb7e78fa05d562e0a5d3089ec896d57d057d38e itself, at which pcs, and in which block range? leads.question: On erigon main, run the frameSlots cache (execution/vm/interpreter.go lines 124-171, instructions.go lines 859-880) with this sequence: an outer PoolManager frame SLOADs pool slot0 in checkPoolInitialized (src/PoolManager.sol:154 or :196), a hook called by beforeModifyLiquidity or beforeSwap calls PoolManager.swap on the same pool, the nested PoolManager frame writes slot0, and the outer frame reads slot0 again in Pool.modifyLiquidity or _swap. Does the outer read return the nested write, and does IntraBlockState.ReadStamp change on writes made by a nested frame of the same contract? Find where IntraBlockState.ReadStamp is defined on erigon main and check that every storage write, every revert to a snapshot and every write by a nested frame of the same contract changes the stamp the cache compares.
leads.why: This reentry is the shape in which a per-frame storage read cache could hand the outer frame a stale price or tick. Any account can build it with a hook on its own pool of real tokens, and the wrong amounts would be paid from the single PoolManager balance. The cache is on main only, so the actor is an operator running a future erigon release.
